# The grid-gui user interface (/gui)

grid-gui has two user interfaces:

* **`/gui/`** — the current one, described here. The page is static HTML, CSS and
  JavaScript modules; the data comes from a small JSON API and the images are drawn by
  the server.
* **`/grid-gui`** — the legacy interface, whose HTML is generated by the C++ code. It is
  kept unchanged while the new interface is being tested, and every old link still works.

`/grid-gui` is a private handler: it accepts only local and private network addresses
by default (see the [developer guide](developer-guide.md#4-startup)). `/gui` is always
private too ([§4](#4-configuration)).

## 1. Using the page

**Data.** Choose the producer, the generation and the parameter; the rest of the
selection (level type, level, forecast type, ensemble member, geometry) offers only what
the chosen parameter has. Each choice keeps as much of the previous selection as still
exists, so switching the generation or the parameter keeps the level and the time.
A list with only one choice is grayed out: it shows the value, which cannot be changed.

* The producer list shows the age of each producer's newest ready generation.
* By default the newest **ready** generation is shown; a generation still being loaded is
  marked *not ready*.
* The parameter list has a filter that matches names, descriptions, units and the other
  names the parameter mappings give to a parameter (for example `Temperature` finds `T-K`).
* A geometry missing from the producer file is marked: queries without an explicit
  geometry do not find it.

**Times and levels.** The time bar shows every time of the field, days in alternating
shades. Hovering a cell previews that time, a click selects it. Next to the image, the
level bar does the same for the levels. Play animates the times; each step waits until
the image has loaded.

**Values.** Hovering the image shows the coordinates, the grid point (i, j) and the value
under the pointer. A click pins the point: the page then shows its time series and, for
fields with several levels, its vertical profile. Clicking a chart selects that time or
level.

**Colours.** The named colours (coastline, land, sea, lat/lon lines, streams) are chosen
from a picker that shows every named colour as a dot at its hue (left to right) and
lightness (top to bottom), the greys in a strip of their own. Overlapping dots are moved
slightly apart. A filter dims the colours whose name does not match; Enter chooses the
first match.

**Zoom.** The mouse wheel zooms the image around the pointer, dragging moves a zoomed
image and a double click shows the whole image. Compared images zoom together. The grid
cells are drawn as sharp squares, so single grid points can be inspected.

**Views.** Image, Map (on the world map), Streams and Animated streams (for direction
fields), Info (the content records and all message attributes, with a filter), sample
value and coordinate tables and the message bytes. The sample tables show a window of
up to 100 × 100 grid points that can be moved over the whole grid; hovering a cell shows
its indexes, coordinates (lat/lon and the grid's own x/y) and value.

**Undefined types.** A forecast type or level type the grid configuration does not
define is shown as *not defined*; its tooltip lists the defined ones.

**Colour maps.** When the values of the field do not fit the range of the chosen colour
map, the legend says so — for example temperatures in °C with a Kelvin colour map — and
offers the colour maps that fit, those named after the quantity first.

The page shows the values as they are stored. Querydata stores temperatures in °C, but
the content is identified with the FMI name T-K; only a query whose parameter mapping has
a conversion function converts them.

**Map area.** The Map view shows the area of the data (its lat/lon bounding box with a
margin) at full resolution, or the whole world. *Download message* saves the GRIB
message.

**Projection.** Image and streams can be drawn in any other geometry (linear
interpolation). *Keep projection* keeps the chosen geometry when the field's own geometry
changes.

**Compare.** *Compare with* shows the same field — the same parameter, level, forecast
type, member, geometry and time — of another generation of the producer, and the
difference B − A with a blue-white-red scale. The hover readout shows A, B and B − A.

**Rendering.** Colour map and opacity, or without a colour map a single hue with the
lowest values brightest; stream line options; lat/lon lines, coastline, land and sea
colours, terrain and sea-depth shading and their order relative to the data. The options
are remembered in the browser. The legend below the image is computed the way the server
colours the image.

**Keyboard.** ← → time, ↑ ↓ level, Home/End first/last time, Space play, c compare,
Esc removes the pinned point, ? shows the keys.

## 2. The parameter key

The key of the selected field is shown exactly as queries use it, for example

```
T-K:MEPS:1093:2:850:1:-1
```

Every part is a button with a tooltip, and *What do the parts mean?* lists them:

| Part | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `T-K` | FMI parameter name, with its description and unit |
| `MEPS` | producer |
| `1093` | geometry: its name, grid size, cell size and corner coordinates |
| `2` | level type, for example pressure |
| `850` | level, in the units of the level type |
| `1` | forecast type, for example deterministic or ensemble |
| `-1` | forecast number (ensemble member), shown only when the key has one |

A query may give four more parts: generation flags, and the area, time and level
interpolation methods. The page shows the methods a query of the key uses: those of the
producer's parameter mapping, or the defaults of the parameter when there is no mapping.
*Copy full form* copies the key with these parts; *Copy TimeSeries URL* copies a
TimeSeries request of the key at the pinned point (or the centre of the grid). When the
server has the data explorer (`/api/explorer` answers), *Open in data explorer* opens the
same request there: the key as a parameter expression of the producer's run at the point,
ready to run, with the meteogram, soundings and the other views of the explorer.

A zero geometry or level type is written as an empty part, as the grid engine writes it.
The geometry's tooltip also gives the lat/lon bounding box of the grid.

## 3. Addresses of the page

The selection is in the address, so a view can be bookmarked or sent, and Back returns
to the previous selection:

```
/gui/?producer=MEPS&generation=20261024T120000&parameter=T-K&levelType=2&level=850
     &forecastType=1&member=-1&geometry=1093&time=20261024T180000
     &view=image&projection=1093&lock=1&compare=20261024T060000&lat=60.2&lon=24.9
     &colormap=...&opacity=200&...
```

Missing parts take their defaults: the newest ready generation, the remembered or a
common parameter, the time nearest to now. The rendering options appear only when they
differ from the defaults.

## 4. Configuration

```
ui :
{
  url       = "/gui"                            # default
  directory = "/usr/share/smartmet/grid-gui"    # default, the files of the page
}
```

`url` must not be `/grid-gui`. An empty `url` disables the new interface.

The URL is private, as `/grid-gui` is: it is not in the URI list of the server, so
frontends do not route it, and it accepts only local and private network addresses unless
`plugins.grid-gui.ip_filters` is set. The page can ask for arbitrarily large areas and long
series, so it is meant for the staff of the site only, not for the public. The `visible`
setting of earlier versions is refused at startup.

## 5. How the page is built

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `grid-gui/Gui.cpp` | Routing below the URL, the files of the page, the rendering URLs |
| `grid-gui/Api.cpp` | The JSON API |
| `grid-gui/Attributes.h` | Session attribute names shared with the legacy code |
| `ui/index.html` | The page skeleton |
| `ui/main.js` | State, address, the data, view and rendering panels, viewer, point charts, keys |
| `ui/selection.js` | Level type → level → forecast type → member → geometry → time from the contents |
| `ui/keyexplain.js` | The parameter key and its explanations |
| `ui/legend.js` | Legends: colour map, hue scale, difference scale (same colours as the server) |
| `ui/charts.js` | SVG line charts for the time series and the profile |
| `ui/timebar.js` | Time and level bars |
| `ui/settings.js` | Rendering options |
| `ui/info.js` | The Info view |
| `ui/sample.js` | The sample value and coordinate tables |
| `ui/colorpicker.js` | The picker of the named colours |
| `ui/api.js`, `ui/dom.js`, `ui/format.js` | Fetching, DOM helpers, formatting |
| `ui/gridgui.css` | Styles, light and dark |

There is no framework and no build step: the files are ES modules loaded as they are.
Text is always set with `textContent`; nothing from the server is inserted as HTML.

The C++ side renders with the same page functions as the legacy interface
(`page_image()` and so on): `gui_render()` builds a session from the readable request
parameters, so both interfaces share the image cache.

## 6. JSON API

All calls are `GET /gui/api/NAME?...`. Errors are `{"error": "..."}` with status 400
(bad request) or 404 (unknown call). Answers may be cached for 5 seconds (`meta` and
`colormap` for 60).

| Call | Parameters | Answer |
|------|------------|--------|
| `meta` | | colours, colour map names and their value ranges (`colorMapRanges`), projections (geometries, `blocked`), the defined forecast and level types, `animationEnabled`, default rendering options |
| `producers` | | `[{id, name, title, description, generations, newest, newestReady}]` |
| `generations` | `producer` (id) | newest first: `[{id, name, analysisTime, ready, start, end, deletion}]` |
| `parameters` | `generation` | `[{name, description, units, fmiId, aliases}]` |
| `contents` | `generation`, `parameter` | `{levelTypes, forecastTypes, geometries (with `bbox`), fields: [{levelId, level, forecastType, forecastNumber, geometry, times[], files[], messages[]}]}` |
| `key` | `file`, `message` | the key and the meaning of its parts, `interpolation`, `aliases`, `searchConfigured` |
| `value` | `file`, `message`, `x`,`y` (0..1 in the image, with `projection`) or `lat`,`lon` | `{value, lat, lon, i, j}` |
| `series` | `generation`, `parameter`, `levelId`, `level`, `forecastType`, `forecastNumber`, `geometry`, `lat`, `lon` | `{times[], values[]}` |
| `profile` | as `series` without `level`, with `time` | `{levelType, levels[], values[]}` |
| `stats` | `file`, `message`, `geometry`, [`projection`], [`file2`, `message2`] | `{count, missing, min, max, mean, step, range}` |
| `colormap` | `name` | `{name, stops: [[value, "AARRGGBB"], ...]}` |
| `info` | `file`, `message` | producer, generation, file and content records, `Attributes: [[name, value], ...]` |
| `sample` | `file`, `message`, [`i0`, `j0`, `size` (1..100, default 50)] | `{columns, rows, i0, j0, values[][], lat[][], lon[][], x[], y[]}`: a window of the grid in data order, `x`/`y` in the grid's own projection |

Missing values are `null`. `stats.step` is the step of the hue scale of an image without
a colour map; `stats.range` is the automatic range of a difference image (the 99th
percentile of the absolute differences).

## 7. Rendering URLs

`/gui/image`, `/gui/map`, `/gui/streams`, `/gui/streamsAnimation`, `/gui/difference`,
`/gui/table`, `/gui/coordinates`, `/gui/message` and `/gui/download` take `file` and
`message`, and the options:

`geometry`, `projection`, `colormap`, `opacity`, `hue`, `saturation`, `blur`,
`coordinateLines`, `landBorder`, `landColor`, `landColorPosition`, `seaColor`,
`seaColorPosition`, `landShadingLight`, `landShadingShadow`, `landShadingPosition`,
`seaShadingLight`, `seaShadingShadow`, `seaShadingPosition`, `missing`, `step`,
`minLength`, `maxLength`, `streamColor`

`difference` also needs `file2` and `message2` (the image is file2 − file) and takes
`range`. `map` takes `area=lon0,lat0,lon1,lat1`: that part of the world at up to 1200
pixels on the longer side (without it the whole world at 1800 × 900). Missing options
take the defaults of `api/meta`.

## 8. Developing the page

Point `ui.directory` at the `ui/` directory of the source tree: the server reads a file
again when it changes, and the page revalidates its files on every load, so a reload in
the browser shows the edit. No restart is needed for anything in `ui/`.

The plugin tests (`make test`, in `test/`) start the grid test database
(`smartmet-grid-test-redis`) and run the requests in `test/input` against the grid test
data, comparing the API answers, the error answers and two images with `test/output`.
For a local server with the same data:

```bash
cd test
mkdir -p tmp                                      # the image cache of the tests
smartmet-grid-test-redis start
cd cnf && smartmetd -c reactor.conf -p 8098       # then open http://localhost:8098/gui/
```

When adding a rendering option, add it to `renderParameters` in `Gui.cpp`, to the
defaults in `api_meta()`, to the views that use it in `ui/settings.js`
(`viewOptions`) and to the cache key of the page function (see the developer guide).
